# Start-ZbxActiveProxy

## SYNOPSIS

Starts an active proxy's uplink as a session: it re-pulls the server's configuration on a cadence, until stopped.

## SYNTAX

```
Start-ZbxActiveProxy [-Name] <string> [-ProxyName] <string> [-Server] <DnsEndPoint[]> [-RefreshInterval <TimeSpan>] [-PassThru] [-Tls <ZabbixTlsMode>] [-PskIdentity <string>] [-Psk <SecureString>] [-Certificate <string>] [-CertificateKey <string>] [-CertificateAuthority <string>] [-CertificateRevocationList <string>] [-ServerIssuer <string>] [-ServerSubject <string>] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

The session is kept in this runspace under -Name and pulls the configuration every -RefreshInterval (60 seconds by default; change it live with Set-ZbxActiveProxy). It uploads history only from data providers registered with Register-ZbxActiveProxyDataProvider; to push history yourself, use Send-ZbxProxyData. Pass -PassThru to write the session. A server that requires TLS from the proxy (its tls_accept) is reached with -PskIdentity and -Psk, or the certificate parameters, as the proxy's own TLSConnect would.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Start an active proxy's uplink

```powershell
Start-ZbxActiveProxy -Name 'uplink' -ProxyName 'proxy-01' -Server 'zabbix.example:10051'
Start-Sleep -Seconds 2
Get-ZbxActiveProxyStatus -Name 'uplink' | Select-Object Name, ProxyName, Version, ConfigRevision, LastPulledAt, Fault
Stop-ZbxActiveProxy -Name 'uplink'
```

The session pulls proxy-01's configuration from the server's trapper now and every -RefreshInterval (60 s by default) until Stop-ZbxActiveProxy. Version is the protocol it speaks: the server's own, adopted from its first refusal. ConfigRevision is 0 before the first pull; Fault holds the last failed pull's error.

### Example 2: Start with a shorter refresh

```powershell
Start-ZbxActiveProxy -Name 'uplink' -ProxyName 'proxy-01' -Server 'zabbix.example:10051' -RefreshInterval '10s' -PassThru |
    Select-Object Name, ProxyName, RefreshInterval
Stop-ZbxActiveProxy -Name 'uplink'
```

-RefreshInterval is a duration ('10s', seconds or a time span; Set-ZbxActiveProxy changes it on a running session); -PassThru writes the session. Several -Server entries are HA nodes, tried in turn.

### Example 3: Push values on every refresh

```powershell
Start-ZbxActiveProxy -Name 'uplink' -ProxyName 'proxy-01' -Server 'zabbix.example:10051' -RefreshInterval '2s'
Register-ZbxActiveProxyDataProvider -Name 'uplink' -ScriptBlock {
    param($config)
    $item = $config.Items.Values | Where-Object Key -eq 'app.requests'
    $now = [DateTimeOffset]::UtcNow
    $value = [Community.Zabbix.Proxy.ZabbixProxyHistoryItem]::new($now.ToUnixTimeMilliseconds(), $item.ItemId, $now, '42')
    [Community.Zabbix.Proxy.ZabbixProxyDataPage]::new([Community.Zabbix.Proxy.ZabbixProxyHistoryItem[]]@($value), $null, $null, $null, $null)
}
Start-Sleep -Seconds 5
Stop-ZbxActiveProxy -Name 'uplink' -WarningAction SilentlyContinue
Get-ZbxItem -Host 'web-01' | Where-Object Key -eq 'app.requests' | Select-Object Key, LastValue
```

The session pushes nothing by itself: a data provider (Register-ZbxActiveProxyDataProvider) returns a page of values before each refresh's upload, and the session sends it as proxy-01 ('proxy data').

## INPUTS

None.

## OUTPUTS

- `ZabbixActiveProxySession`: Represents an active proxy's uplink kept running as a session: it re-pulls the configuration on -RefreshInterval, over a ZabbixProxyUplink built with no DI container — the SDK type composes over a plain .
